what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to approve the Lunenburg High School ice hockey trip to Waterville Valley.

A line-item transfer from grounds supplies to contract, to remove hazardous dead trees at the primary school, was presented with a recommendation to approve; the minutes record discussion only, no vote.
The trip's meals are covered by boosters and fundraising, including an alumni game, so students pay only spending money.
The superintendent said the state foundation budget report finds the formula out of step with actual costs, notably health insurance and special education.
Minutes were considered approved with no objections, and a special town meeting was noted for Monday, November 16.

why_it_matters: The foundation budget formula sets how much state school aid the district is judged to need, so a gap in health insurance and special education costs bears on how much falls to the local budget, mostly taxes.
The tree-removal transfer moves money within the existing school budget and does not add to it, but the minutes show no vote on it, so residents cannot tell from them whether it was approved.
